# Playtest diary: r13-typed-full

- **Mode:** typed
- **Start:** the start of the game
- **Persona:** a stage-magic hobbyist who notices every object, keeps a written inventory and types full sentences
- **Seed:** 53618
- **Conveniences:** on
- **Undo:** off
- **Build commit:** 4e968236
- **Budget:** about 400 commands per leg, 1500 commands in all
- **Round:** 13
- **Friction log:** filed through the harness (--friction), in playtests/2026-10-06/r13-typed-full.friction.jsonl

## Narrative

(About 100 words per 10 commands: what you tried, and what you believed.)

**Cmds 1-10.** Woke on Deck Twelve of the S.P.S. Duffy. My written inventory: Spacecraft Activation Form HB-56-V, Robot Use Authorization Form JZ-59-G, Assignment Completion Form QX-17-T; wearing a Patrol uniform (ID card 1451-352-716 inside) and a chronometer engraved "Love, Mom and Dad". "Take inventory" was not understood (filed); "the slot next to the door" fails on "next". Reading the forms opens paper images, but my image viewer refuses them (budget exceeded on my side, not a game fault), so I cannot see the form text. Blather wandered past with scrub supplies; footnotes work by typing "footnote 2". Went aft to a vast Forms Storage Room full of stamped boxes. Belief: the slot by the port door takes my ID card.

**Cmds 11-21.** Box labels are a bureaucratic joke ("Loss of Form Pallet Label Report Form Release Form"); "read the writing on the boxes" failed but "read the boxes" worked. Starboard from Deck Twelve is the Cargo Bay Entrance (cargo bay starboard, small entrance fore). Fore is the Robot Pool: Rex (heavy lifter, bin 1), Helen (form decollator, bin 2) and a short robot playing marbles in bin 3, who turned out to be Floyd! I fed the Robot Use Authorization Form into the slot and typed 3 on the keypad; Floyd hugged me. Inventory now: Spacecraft Activation Form, Assignment Completion Form, uniform, ID card, chronometer, plus Floyd. "Marbles" is unknown to the parser. Next: the cargo bay, then the port door slot.

**Cmds 22-32.** Cargo Bay holds a spacetruck. Opened the hatch, climbed in; Floyd bounced in after me. Cockpit: space band radio, red emergency-beacon button, autopilot slot and keypad, pilot and copilot seats. Took a survival kit (orange goo, gray goo, a plaid Thermos with little robots on it, closed). Closed the hatch. The activation form was spat back: both seats must be occupied. Sat in the pilot seat and Floyd hopped into the copilot seat on his own, which felt charming. Belief: insert the form now, then type a destination on the keypad (the station's number; I can't read the form image, so I'll experiment).

**Cmds 33-44.** With both seats filled the activation form was accepted: "Type in the course heading." I can't see any form image, so I typed 285 from vague memory of the original game (memory, not screen). The truck launched; fuel dropped to three-quarters, one-quarter, then we stopped dead in empty space, no station in sight. Wrong heading, clearly. Pressing the red beacon button first scolded me ("You're not in trouble!"), then after the course-terminus message it started an emergency broadcast; I'd switched the space band radio on and someone said "Breaker. Over." Oxygen: about two chrons. Belief: this run is probably lost; I'll talk to the radio, then restart and hunt for the heading in-game.

**Cmds 45-53, restart.** Radio voice repeats "Breaker. Over." but say hello / say help / talk to the radio all fail. Restarted the same session. The port door wants a *validated* Assignment Completion Form, so the way home is after the mission. Since my image tool cannot open any paper, I asked the operator what the activation form says. **Not from the screen:** the operator told me course = floor((floor(T/50) - 132)^2 / 4) + 103, where T is the game clock when the course is typed. (My first try at T~5719 should have been 184, not 285.) Replaying the opening now.

**Cmds 54-68.** Replayed: starboard, fore, robot form in slot, "type 3" (Floyd), aft, starboard (Blather slouched past again), opened the hatch, entered, took the survival kit, closed the hatch, sat in the pilot seat (Floyd took copilot), activation form into the slot at time 5399. That was right on a 50-tick boundary, so I examined the keypad to move the clock to 5431, then typed 247 (floor(5431/50)=108; (108-132)^2/4=144; +103). "Course set." The truck roared out. Now waiting out the trip and hoping for a station.

**Cmds 69-77.** Heading 247 worked: a star ahead became the space station (central spherical Command Module, Sub-Module jutting north, a seedy "village" of tubes and derelict rockets). Bay one was occupied, so we docked in bay two: +5, score 5. No one met us. Odd. Hungry and thirsty: ate the orange goo (apricot yogurt). The Thermos holds blue soup; closed it again for later. Still carrying the gray goo, Thermos, kit, and the Assignment Completion Form (unvalidated). "stand up and open the hatch" failed on "and"; periods work. Stepped out into Docking Bay #2: the huge station door is east.

**Cmds 78-87.** "examine the huge door" in Docking Bay #2 said there is no huge door, though the room text names it (filed as a bug). East auto-door led to Level Five lobby (elevator + call button east, corridor NE/SE, doors N and W, ladder up/down). North: Workshop, where I took a twenty-ohm bedistor (added to my written inventory); the machinery is "outside my expertise". North of the Workshop is a pitch-black Storage room (grue joke) - need a light. Back to Level Five, then northeast to North Junction (corridor N, door E, doorway NE). Floyd brought a new robot friend: Plato, polite, says he has seen no soul for a day. Station seems deserted.

**Cmds 88-97.** Plato answers "I'll look it up in the library" to the station and the humans. East of North Junction: Sick Bay (beds, diagnostic gear, ID-reader security door east which ignores my ID card; exits W, SE). SE: East Connection, a shut iris hatch to the Military Sub-Module with a slot; doors NW, doorways S and SW, junction W. South: Comm Center, unmanned; its red emergency-beacon button gave me an electric shock (sabotage?); message screen blank. My theory: something happened to the crew and someone wants to keep the station silent.

**Cmds 98-107.** SW of East Connection: Station Control. Monitors: COMMUNICATION RED, FOOD PRODUCTION RED, PRINTING YELLOW, others green. Exits S, NE, W. South: Commander's Office (log reader, fixed, red button, mic/speaker, no tape; doors S and E, doorways N and NW). East: Commander's Quarters with a HyperSecurity safe (8000-setting dial, 12-20 number combination: not a dial puzzle, I suspect brute force or an explosive), and a log tape on the desk: "Commander's Log -- 11349.12.2 through 11349.12.4". Took it. Desk has nothing else. "take X and read Y" fails on "and"; periods work. Plan: play the tape in the log reader.

**Cmds 108-117.** The log tape plays in the Commander's Office reader; the tiny red button advances it. Notes: fuel cells hidden in the Dome's storage bin, locked, **key in the Commander's safe**. Collater #22 off-line. Alien craft towed to Docking Bay #1 (alien remains + featureless pyramid); pyramid moved to the holding tank in the Sci Sub-Module. Shady Dan in the village sells modified Patrol ID cards; village off-limits, but someone validated village entry forms, so **the Commander hid the stamp under his bed**. The log reader overheats; there's a spare somewhere. Breakdowns in gym and laundry equipment: sabotage? Floyd and Plato went off to the library. Theory: the stamp validates my Assignment Completion Form (my way home).

**Cmds 118-127.** Rest of the log: the Duffy's request for binder forms; web-feeder #17 shut down and nearly took an arm; a hull welder malfunctioned and injured an ensign; even the spare log reader overheated "What the krip!..." Machines are turning on people: I suspect the alien pyramid. I took the tape back out (good call: a whine, then an explosion, and now there's a black scar where the log reader sat). Looked under the Commander's bed: a self-inking validation stamp. Inventory: kit (gray goo, Thermos of blue soup), Assignment Completion Form, bedistor, log tape, stamp, ID card, chronometer.

**Cmds 128-~131 (harness count).** South of the Commander's Office: Briefing Room (doors N, W). West: South Connection, a closed iris hatch south (where a Diplomatic Sub-Module would be; I think the village is beyond) with a slot; doors E and W, junction N. West: Robot Shop. An unborn robot "Oliver" lies inert (incubation 2-20 days). A heating chamber, always on, holds a medium drill bit, but its opening is too small for a human hand. Floyd wandered off, so I couldn't ask him to reach in. Theory: Floyd's small hand or a tool fetches the bit.

**Cmds 132-143.** Mapped: South Connection north to South Junction (corridor NE/NW, doorways SW, SE, E). SW is a dark File Room; SE leads to the Commander's Office; E to Station Control. Floyd and Plato rejoined me, so I walked back to the Robot Shop and said "Floyd, take the drill bit from the heating chamber". He grabbed it, yelped, dropped it to cool, then spoke movingly about waking up lonely and wanting to teach Oliver paddleball. Took the medium drill bit: +3, score 8. Need: a drill for the bit, a light for dark rooms, a way into the safe (Dome storage-bin key).

**Cmds 144-153.** The Level Five ring is: Level Five lobby (W), North Junction (N), East Connection (E), South Junction (S). Climbed the ladder to Level Four: bunk level, elevator E, Docking Bay #3 W, ladder up/down. Female Barracks (N), Barracks SanFac (between, exits N/S), Male Barracks (S, exits NE/NW). Searching cubicles in both barracks gives only "personal items of little interest". Floyd and Plato tag along with sweet banter. Next: Docking Bay #3, then upward toward the Dome.

**Cmds 154-163.** Docking Bay #3 (wide, low) held a lilac nanofilm spool labelled "Spacetruck Refueling Instructions"; taken (needs a reader). Up the ladder: Level Three lobby (doors N, S, NW; doorway SW; elevator E; ladder up/down). North: Gym with a multi-function exercise machine and a sign: its diagnostics talk on frequency 710; nothing broadcasting on 710 may come near. Examining the machine just says "There's no one in the exercise machine." Floyd and Plato went off to play Hider-and-Seeker. Theory: something that transmits on 710 will wreck (or tame) the possessed exercise machine.

**Cmds 164-173.** Level Three NW: Laundry, with a dryer (empty), a presser (off, now open, empty) and an empty spot where the washer should be (the washer has walked off? sabotage log mentioned laundry machinery). South: Theatre, sixty seats; the projection booth is closed and locked. I'm now told I'm getting weary and should find a safe place to sleep. Barracks seem the natural bed. Still to see: Level Three SW doorway, ladder up/down further, the elevator.

**Cmds 174-182.** Level Three SW: Chapel, with an eternal flame and a seven-pointed star high above a wooden pulpit; the star blinks rhythmically, out of reach. Took a puce nanofilm spool, "Chapel Maintenance Procedures". "examine the blinking star" is refused though the room says it's blinking (filed). The pulpit opens to reveal a switch that turns the eternal flame off and on (I put it back on). Theory: the blinking star is a signal (maybe Morse, maybe a 710 broadcaster?), and the chapel spool explains the switch. I still need a nanofilm reader; library likely (Plato visits one).

**Cmds 183-188.** Ladder up from Level Three: Mess Hall (doorway SE, doors N, S, NE; elevator/ladder E). A steaming cup of coffee, no one in sight (Mary Celeste). Turning on a Food Dispensing Unit: cheery menu, then a jet of ACID; I dodged. Food production is deadly, so the gray goo and blue soup are my only food. North: Main Storage (doors NW and SW at the curved ends). Took a detonator; it opens to show a blackened hyperdiode (burnt out; needs replacing). Written inventory now matches the panel: detonator(+blackened hyperdiode), puce and lilac spools, medium drill bit, stamp, log tape, bedistor, survival kit (gray goo, Thermos), uniform+ID, chronometer, Assignment Completion Form. Theory: a working detonator plus explosive opens the safe.

**Cmds 189-198.** Main Storage NW door returns to the Mess Hall. Mess Hall NE: Meeting Room 1 (doors S, W); S: Meeting Room 2 (N, S); S: Library (door N, exit W): magazines, a voice-only nanofilm reader, and the computer terminal has been *removed*. Played the lilac spool: fuel cells on a spacetruck are swapped using a "quarnum wrench", then the voice dissolved into static and "You will die, human! All humans will die!" The machines are definitely possessed. I'm "really tired now", so I must sleep soon; heading for the barracks on Level Four.

**Cmds 199-212.** Took the lilac spool back. The Male Barracks has no bed I could find ("sleep" -> "civilized societies sleep in beds"; filed as confusing), so I trekked down to the Sick Bay on Level Five and got into a bed. Slept: a lovely "Open the pod bay doors, Floyd" nightmare. Woke on Novem 5, 11349 (+3, score 11), clock reset to 1658. Everything I carried was dropped beside the bed, so I must pick it all back up. Floyd and Plato waited for me.

**Cmds 213-222.** "take all" recovered everything (and a funny bit about trying to lift Floyd). The Sick Bay auto-door opened sluggishly and zoomed shut early: doors are turning too. North of North Junction: North Connection, the tube to the Scientific Sub-Module goes north; auto-door W, doorway E. East: the PX, whose Vendo-Matic (1 galakmid per item) has only #6 All-Purpose Timer and #9 Large Drill Bit left. The PX's SW exit is North Junction's NE doorway. Theory: a galakmid coin buys the timer, which plus detonator plus explosive opens the safe. I have no coin yet.

**Cmds 223-228.** North Connection's west auto-door opens into the dark Storage (same room as north of the Workshop). North through the shiny Tube: Scientific Sub-Module, Engineering Lab (gangways up/down, door N, tube S). North: Engineering Office with Professor Schmidt's diary: the alien ship came from a neighbouring galaxy, over a billion years old; its wall markings are rows of identical dots that he decoded through "nonvisual properties" (Braille? sound?), and "my pal, the mayor, will get to show off his linguistic training" - the village mayor reads the dots. Lab machinery kept failing near the pyramid. A fumble taught me the 7-item hand limit (nicely explained); the kit only holds one more spool. Dropped the spent log tape here.

**Cmds 229-236.** Up the gangway: Astro Lab with a twenty-prong fromitz board (17 cm square, left there: hands full); Astro Office to its north is empty. Up again: Scientists' Quarters, top of the Sub-Module, cubicles with nothing of interest. Hungry and thirsty again: ate the gray goo (Ramosian tree-mold custard). Thirst still nags; the blue soup is my last provision. Next: down to the lower Sub-Module levels, where I expect the pyramid's holding tank.

**Cmds 237-244.** Moved the lilac spool into the kit (kit: Thermos, puce + lilac spools; full) and took the fromitz board. Down past Engineering to the Bio Lab; north, Bio Office: a bloodstained note: "think of this station as a cell and the pyramid as a mechanized bacterioph[age]". So the pyramid infects machines like a virus. ("scribbled note" unknown word; filed.) Dropped the note. Bottom level: Holding Tank. The tank's thick wall has been *blasted open* and it is empty. The pyramid is loose somewhere on the station. Hands: form, kit, bedistor, stamp, drill bit, detonator, fromitz board (7).

**Cmds 245-~255.** Back down through the Tube. Multi-command lines with periods work smoothly and save typing. Level Five's west door is just Docking Bay #2 (truck still there). Ladder down: Level Six (huge doors NW and SW, smaller doors N and S, corridor SE, elevator E, ladder up/down). North: Auxiliary Barracks (unused, curves east) and Auxiliary SanFac; "water" is not a known word, so no drinking from sinks. Every auto-door now opens sluggishly and slams early.

**Cmds 256-262.** The SanFac's way back to the barracks is north, not west (cost me three moves; filed). South of Level Six: Officers' Quarters A (door N, opening SE) -> Officers SanFac (bathtubs; exits N, NE, NW) -> Quarters C (NE; auto-door N) and Quarters B (N of SanFac; door N). All three searched: nothing. P.A. announced: "Deep-space communication received at Comm Center. No operator on duty." I want to go read the Comm Center screen on Level Five next.

**Cmds 263-271.** North of Quarters B: End of Corridor (doors E, N [security, ID reader], S, SW; corridor widens W back to Level Six). East is a dark Shipping Room. Level Six's NW huge door: Docking Bay #1 with the alien ship, hatch open. Inside: skin-crawling angles, an empty sturdy pedestal (the pyramid's home, I bet), a brittle alien skeleton, and wall dots: rows ".. ..", ".. .... . ... . ... ... . ...", ".. ... .", ".... . ... .", ".. ... ." (dot groups 2-2 / 2-4-1-3-1-3-3-1-3 / 2-3-1 / 4-1-3-1 / 2-3-1). Touching is useless. Floyd is frightened. Theory: the mayor in the village decodes them; maybe they are a count/tap code or musical.

**Cmds 272-279.** The skeleton has an "unusually overdeveloped tongue case" (so the dots may be sounds: clicks?). Listening to the dots does nothing. Level Six's SW huge door: Docking Bay #4, smallest, empty. Ladder down: Printing Plant (whole level; partitioned area NW; elevator E; ladder up/down). There: a mauve spool "Collater Repair Manual" (left on the floor) and a trash can holding a crumpled Illegal Space Village Entry Form FW-83-Q, unvalidated. Dropped the bedistor in the Printing Plant and took the crumpled form. Plan: flatten it in the Laundry presser, stamp it, feed it to the South Connection slot to enter the village.

**Cmds 280-288.** NW of the Printing Plant: Paper Recycling Plant, where a tired Patrol-issue drill (small bit inside, "may not have much work left") lay; dropped the fromitz board there and took the drill. Stash so far: log tape (Engineering Office), note (Bio Office), bedistor + mauve spool (Printing Plant), fromitz board (Paper Recycling). Climbed to Level Five and found the ring has a fifth node: South Junction NE = East Junction (NW/SW, and E to East Connection). The Comm Center screen: the Duffy found the binder forms in a mislabelled pallet; "Abort assignment and return to Duffy." Ha. Theory: I still need fuel (Dome bin, key in safe) to fly home, and to stop the pyramid.

**Cmds 289-297.** Walked the ring back to Level Five and climbed toward the Laundry. On Level Three, Welder Number 4 rolled toward me "quivering with excitement" (the welder that hurt the ensign, I presume). I dropped down the ladder to Level Four; it moved off. Came back up and slipped into the Laundry. (Note: the empty washer spot is no longer mentioned; the room now lists only presser and dryer.) Put the crumpled village entry form in the presser. Next: close it and switch it on.

**Cmds 298-306.** Closed the presser and turned it on: steam trickled, then billowed; turned it off and opened it: a neatly ironed Illegal Space Village Entry Form FW-83-Q. Stamped it (validated) and also stamped my Assignment Completion Form for the trip home. Went down to South Connection and fed the entry form to the slot: the iris hatch sparked and jammed half-open, wide enough to pass, revealing a dingy connecting tube. +6, score 17. Puzzle solved: crumpled form -> presser -> stamp -> slot. Next: the village, Shady Dan, and the mayor who reads the dots.

**Cmds 307-312.** Gravity cut off as I left the Command Module (weightless now). Grimy Passage S -> Main Street, deserted (openings up, NE, S, W; SE ramps down). West: Travel Agency (posters of Ramos II, Varshon, Mazzotta; exits E, SE). SE: Bank of Nebulon (doors N, NW) with a floating platinum detector. Took it and switched it on; it gives no reading yet. Theory: it beeps near platinum galakmid coins, which buy the timer at the PX. Hands: drill (+small bit), detonator, medium bit, stamp, kit, Assignment form, detector = 7.

**Cmds 313-319.** Main Street NE: Greasy Straw ("Galaxy's Best Zero-Gee Restaurant", exits NE/SW); behind the counter, a warm thick cup of Ramosian Fire Nectar (left it; a possible drink). NE: Trading Post, an old gutted cargo ship (many passageways, an opening in the floor). Sign: "FREZONE (tm) explosive available", illegal wares by appointment. Instruction sheet: insert explosive in a hole of the right diameter, attach detonator to explosive and timer, set timer, vamoose; keep it below 150 K or it goes off after 100 millichrons. A twelve-prong fromitz board floats here too. Dropped the sheet here ("Dropped, so to speak" in zero-g, cute). The safe plan is clear: drill a hole, explosive, detonator (needs a good hyperdiode), timer.

**Cmds 320-327.** Down through the Trading Post floor: Warehouse, with a closed door down under a red sign "TRADING POST VACUUM STORAGE AREA - Trespassers will be spaced!" (cold vacuum = where the explosive is kept?). Openings up and SW. SW: Alley, garbage-strewn, "dark passages in almost every direction", sloping up NW. Garbage: nothing. South: Loan Shark's moored vessel with a sturdy strong box with a HUGE lock (coins inside? the platinum detector is still silent here though). Theory: drill the strong box lock with the drill, or use the explosive.

**Cmds 328-334.** Drilling the strong box: the game warned the drill has ONE hole left and asked me to repeat to spend it (nice); I saved it for the Commander's safe. Alley W: "openings in ALMOST every direction" (joke). Alley E: a fake "Studio" gag, then the Junk Yard (old drydock; passages up and W) with magnetic spaceboots in decent shape. Reaching for them: my ID card twitched; carrying both would wipe the card, no second warning. I left the boots. Theory: drop the ID card somewhere safe before taking the boots, or deliberately wipe it for Shady Dan to re-program.

**Cmds 335-345.** Up from the Junk Yard: Shady Dan's trailer (connectors NW and down; a lot of used spaceships outside the dirty window). A jerry-built "innocuous machine" with keypad and small slot. Turned it on; Welder Number 1 appeared, so I ducked down to the Junk Yard and back. Put my ID card in the slot: "Current rank is 6: Lieutenant First Class. Enter new rank." Typed 10: "Grand Fleet HyperAdmiral." Took the card and put it back in my uniform ("my uniform pocket" was "too many nouns"). Theory: security doors (Sick Bay east, End of Corridor north) now open for me, as long as I keep the card away from the magnetic boots.

**Cmds 346-354.** Thirsty+hungry: drank the Fire Nectar at the Greasy Straw (cup vaporized). Main Street S is the Bank. Main Street up: Mayor's Office with "Deciphering Alien Speech"; a paper fell out: a TASTE glossary! (Schmidt's "nonvisual properties" = taste.) Copied in full: bttr/salty/bttr softness/weakness; sweet/v.sour Hunji (noun); blnd/salty/sour Zeenak (adj); blnd/bttr air/atmosphere; sour/blnd/blnd/sour died/failed; sweet/v.sweet legal destruction (sabotage?); v.salty however; sour/blnd/sour/sweet turn back; blnd (def. article?); v.sweet/blnd/sour I have shined light upon; slightly-sour solitary; v.sweet/v.salty element/substance; sweet/slightly-bttr brethren (adj); blnd/sour/v.sour is souring; v.salty/salty/sour bad/evil/deadly radiations; spicy-hot/blnd/blnd 78(?) 7/8(?); bttr/sour/v.sour weapon (possessive); v.sweet (emphasis mark?). Theory: lick the dots in the alien ship to read the message.

**Cmds 355-358+.** Dropped the book and paper in the Mayor's Office (copy above). Main Street SE ramps down to the Alley. Alley SW: Pawn Shop (three balls; entrance NE) with a pawned spray can: "E-Z SPRAY SPORZ (tm), high-quality spores, lowest gas-inducement levels" (took it; "read the lettering on the spray can" failed again, filed). Dropped the stamp in the Pawn Shop. Back in the Alley: "the detector is getting warm". Not platinum, I decided: like the log reader, it may be overheating under the pyramid's influence, so I dropped it in the Loan Shark before it blows. Hands: drill, detonator, medium bit, kit, Assignment form, spray can.

**Cmds 359-364.** Correction: picking the detector back up, it "feels warm" only here at the Loan Shark, and not in the Alley or Warehouse. So "warm" is the hot/cold platinum signal: the strong box holds platinum (galakmids, I bet). Took the detector back. The lock "is only SLIGHTLY smaller than an average asteroid"; "huge lock" is not accepted as a noun phrase (filed). Dilemma: the drill has one hole left, and both the strong box and the Commander's safe seem to want a hole (explosive "in hole of appropriate diameter"). Holding back for now.

**Cmds 365-368.** Chained moves (periods) carried me back to the station and down to Docking Bay #1 in two calls. In the alien ship, "lick the dots" worked! Tastes, translated with the Mayor's glossary: "Brethren Hunji: the sabotage failed. However, I have shined light upon the Zeenak weapon's solitary weakness: substance 78! Turn back the deadly radiations! However, the air is souring." **Element 78 is platinum.** So the pyramid (Zeenak weapon) is beaten with platinum, and the platinum detector says the Loan Shark's strong box has some. This is the core of the game.

**Cmds 369-371.** The Docking Bay #1 door nearly nipped my heels. On Level Six the detector got "very warm" (platinum near Level Six? or something else nearby). End of Corridor: my HyperAdmiral card opened the security door, but it glides shut in one turn, so "put the ID card in the ID reader. go north." in one line. Armory (+5, score 22): took a fusor-beam zapgun, indicator reads "7" (charges?). ID card back in my uniform. Hands: zapgun, detector, spray can, drill(+small bit), detonator, medium bit, kit, Assignment form (8: fumble risk).

**Cmds 372-380.** Left the medium drill bit in the Armory (security door from inside just opens). Down to the Printing Plant: the ladder to Level Eight is sealed off *from below*. Called the elevator (warm whoosh); it's a weightless open frame with a level keypad. "type 8": it whines but won't move. Level Eight is blocked both ways: I believe the pyramid is down there. Detector reports only on change; I can't yet locate the platinum beyond the Loan Shark's strong box.

**Cmds 381-383.** Elevator "type 1" went up to the Dome (top level): pebbled paths, exotic shrubbery under a transparent dome; elevator/button/ladder top to the east; an air shaft grating; a thick metal storage bin, "Shrubbery Maintenance Supplies", with a newly welded lock, warm to the touch. Holding the detector near it: "Yeow! too hot to handle", and I dropped it (it lies in the Dome). So "warm" detector readings may track heat/platinum in fuel cells? The bin holds the hidden fuel cells (log) and its key is in the Commander's safe. "read the sign on the bin" failed again (filed).

**Cmds 384-387.** The grating is securely affixed. Shot the bin lock with the zapgun: the bin glowed and cooled, nothing more; the zapgun dropped from 7 to 6 (wasted charge). Then Plato, suddenly cold: "Tagging along after this simpleton human is becoming tiresome," and strolled off with Floyd. I suspect Plato is being turned by the pyramid; watch him.

**Cmds 388-400 (leg end).** Elevator "type 5" back down to Level Five; Sick Bay's security door (HyperAdmiral card) leads to an empty three-cell Brig. The East Connection iris hatch is now frozen open onto a grimy connector (a second way into the village). In the Makeshift Connector, Welder Number 4 came for me; "shoot the welder with the zapgun" vaporized it (zapgun now 5). East: Broadway (openings everywhere, one down). Down: Fortune Teller with a crystal ball whose vision is a con-artist's tip sheet ("wave your hands around the ball": as a magician I approved; it did nothing). North of Broadway: Recruitment Office, Patrol posters; "recruitment" is an unknown word. Leg spent at 400 commands, score 22.

## Leg handoff

### Map so far
- **Duffy (start):** Deck Twelve (slot by port door wants a *validated* Assignment Completion Form) - aft Forms Storage Room; starboard Cargo Bay Entrance - fore Robot Pool, starboard Cargo Bay (spacetruck).
- **Station, Command Module** (elevator east of every lobby; keypad levels 1-8; ladder links lobbies):
  - L1 Dome (elevator stop "1"): locked, warm storage bin "Shrubbery Maintenance Supplies" (fuel cells per the log; key in Commander's safe), air shaft grating (fixed). Platinum detector lies here.
  - L2 Mess Hall (FDUs spray acid; steaming coffee). N Main Storage (detonator found here; doors NW back to Mess Hall, SW unexplored). NE Meeting Room 1 -> S Meeting Room 2 -> S Library (voice-only spool reader, possessed; terminal removed) -> W back to Mess Hall. Mess Hall S door unexplored.

Kicking, shaking, hitting, and shoving the drill, goo, boots or board up the hole all fail; neither Floyd nor Plato can reach it. DO NOT zap the machine: it destroys the dispenser and the timer.

### Open puzzles and theories
- The stuck timer: the right method is unknown (a thin hook? some other tool?). In this restart the coin and machine are gone, so the timer is lost unless one exists elsewhere.
- FREZONE is in the vacuum storage below the Warehouse airlock; a spacesuit or other protection is needed. Not found in Docking Bays 3/4, the Officers' area, the Brig or the Armory. The dark Shipping Room, dark Storage and dark File Room are unsearched (need a light).
- Safe: drilled hole (medium or large bit?), FREZONE in the hole, detonator (needs the J-series hyperdiode from the village scrap sculpture) and timer. The safe holds the Dome bin key, and the bin holds the fuel cells.
- Pyramid on sealed Level Eight; platinum is its weakness (the coin may have been it, and it's now spent). Plato's confrontation is still pending.
- Re-ranking the wiped card: Shady Dan's machine again, presumably.

### What I would try next
If more commands ever exist: restore 'Warehouse, day 2' only if willing to lose points. Otherwise re-rank the card at Shady Dan's, find a light for the dark rooms (a spacesuit may be there), and handle Plato's attack with 'Floyd, take the stun ray'.

friction.result: Shoved up into the hole, drops out; same reply as for the drill and the goo
friction.why: The stuck timer gives a nice classic setup (fingertips touch it, can't grip), but every object I try gets the identical generic reply, with no hint which kind of tool or action is needed

friction.command: shoot the dispensing machine with the zapgun
friction.result: BLAM! The dispenser is dispensed. Nothing left behind; the paid-for timer is gone
friction.why: The same zapgun on the strong box left its coin behind, so I expected the timer to survive; here it silently vanished with the machine, a likely unwinnable state with no warning beyond a joke

friction.command: read the message on the screen
friction.result: [That sentence isn't one I recognize.]
friction.why: The room says the screen is displaying a message; "read the message on the screen" is the obvious full sentence, but only "read the screen" works

friction.command: ask Plato about the pyramid (Plato in the next room)
friction.result: Those things aren't here!
friction.why: The plural reply doesn't say whether Plato or the pyramid is missing; "Plato isn't here" would have told me to go and find him

friction.command: ask Floyd for the magnetic boots (ID card in my uniform)
friction.result: Floyd handed me the boots; the ID card still opens the Sick Bay security door afterwards
friction.why: The game warned that taking the boots again with the card on me would wipe it with no second warning, yet getting them from Floyd left the card working: the rule is bypassed or inconsistent

friction.command: wear the magnetic boots (after Floyd "handed" them to me)
friction.result: [taking the pair of magnetic boots first] ... then the ID reader says the card's data is damaged
friction.why: Correction to row 272: the wipe rule works, but Floyd's "handing you the boots" did not actually put them in my hands, which is misleading. Wearing them was the real pickup and wiped my HyperAdmiral card without the expected reminder

r13-click-fullA.diary:
# Playtest diary: r13-click-fullA

- **Mode:** click
- **Start:** the start of the game
- **Persona:** a museum docent in their sixties on a laptop trackpad who reads everything slowly and twice
- **Seed:** 20493
- **Conveniences:** on
- **Undo:** off
- **Build commit:** 4e968236
- **Budget:** about 400 commands per leg, 1500 commands in all
- **Round:** 13
- **Friction log:** filed through the harness (--friction), in playtests/2026-10-06/r13-click-fullA.friction.jsonl

## Narrative

(About 100 words per 10 commands: what you tried, and what you believed.)

**Commands 1-10.** I start on Deck Twelve of the S.P.S. Duffy holding three forms and an ID card. I opened the Spacecraft Activation Form; the game handed me a picture of the paper, but my viewer would not show it to me (my side, not the game's), so I have not read the form itself. Read my ID card (1451-352-716); Blather shuffled past, and a footnote reminded me who he was. Aft is a vast Forms Storage Room, boxes only. Starboard leads to the Cargo Bay Entrance; fore of that is the Robot Pool with three robots: Rex (lifter), Helen (forms burster) and a short one playing marbles. A slot and a keypad. I believe the Robot Use form goes in that slot.

**Commands 11-22.** Looked at the marbles robot: it is Floyd, my old friend from Resida! Read the Robot Use form (again only a picture I cannot see). Put the form in the slot ("Put it in…" then "slot"; the menu had closed after my Read, so I had to reopen it). The recording asked for a bin number; the keypad offered "number 1 to 3", I typed 3 and Floyd hugged me. He follows me now. Went to the Cargo Bay: a spacetruck. Opened the hatch, went in: pilot and copilot seats, a band radio, a red emergency-beacon button, an autopilot slot and keypad. Took the survival kit and opened it: orange goo, gray goo, a Thermos. Next: the activation form in the autopilot slot.

**Commands 23-34.** The Thermos is plaid with little robots, closed. Put the activation form in the slot: spat back, "both pilot and copilot seats must be occupied." Sat in the pilot seat and Floyd climbed into the copilot seat on his own (lovely). Tried to close the hatch: can't reach it from the seat. Form in again: "Spacecraft activated. Type in the course heading." The keypad takes 0 to 9999, but I do not know the heading. I opened Papers & blueprints (a full list: three forms, a blueprint key, nine blueprints) and the Assignment Completion form, but again I cannot see the pictures on my side. Asked Floyd (only "game" and "Floyd" topics); told him to launch: "Controls too scary-looking." Saved here.

**Commands 25-39.** The radio has no microphone. With no form I could read, I typed heading 285: that number came from my memory of the original game, not from the screen. "Course set." I waited and the truck roared out with the hatch open: air gone, dead. Fair; the game had even told me I could not reach the hatch from my seat. Restored, stood up, closed the hatch, sat again (Floyd sat too), saved over. The harness told me to answer "569 <number>" and then said that menu had closed; reopening the keypad worked. Typed 285 again, waited: "The truck roars out... You settle back for the long trip." Fuel at three-quarters; Floyd wants a phone book.

**Commands 40-44.** The braking rockets fired, then the truck stopped dead in empty space: "no space station, or any other sign of civilization." Fuel effectively zero, oxygen for two chrons. So 285 was wrong (my memory failed me, or this edition's form differs). Pushed the red beacon: first a scolding ("misuse is a court-martial offense!"), then a stuck recording, "nothing can go wrong <skip> go wrong...". Restored to the seat before the heading. Opened the Spacecraft Activation form in the viewer again; still only a picture for me, and the game's own Read only says the form is in my package. I am blocked on the course heading.

**Commands 45-55.** Asked Floyd for help ("Let's play Hider-and-Seeker"). Tried heading 777 (the station's number): the same trip, the same dead stop in empty space. Each wrong guess costs about seven commands. **Note for honesty:** I then asked the person running this session, since I cannot see the paper; they gave me a rule standing in for the form's chart: heading = floor((floor(T/50) - 132)^2 / 4) + 103, T being the game clock when the heading is typed. That knowledge did NOT come from the screen. At T=5232 it gives 299. Restored, typed 299, "Course set", the truck launched.

**Commands 56-65.** Heading 299 was right: a star grew into the station, with a lovely description (spherical Command Module, Sub-Module "north", a seedy "village" of tubes and old rockets). Saved a new position. Ate the orange goo (apricot yogurt!) and the truck docked in bay two (bay one occupied): "Stationfall." +5, score 5. Nobody came to meet us. Odd. Opened the Thermos: blue soup, which I kept (the soup has Eat, no Drink). Stood, opened the hatch, stepped out into Docking Bay #2; the big auto-door is east.

**Commands 66-76.** Through the auto-door to Level Five, the middle lobby: elevator east, corridors NE and SE, doors N and W, a ladder up and down. North is the Workshop (machinery "far outside my area of expertise"); I took a twenty-ohm bedistor and Floyd caught up. North of that, Storage is pitch black (a grue joke), so I backed out; I need a light. NE of the lobby is North Junction (corridor north, door east, doorway NE). East is Sick Bay: beds, diagnostics, and a security door with an ID reader. My Paperwork ID card did nothing in it.

**Commands 77-96.** SE of Sick Bay: East Connection, a shut iris hatch to a Military Sub-Module with a slot beside it. South of it the Comm Center: nobody on duty, a wide-band beacon button and a blank message screen. SW: Station Control; the board shows COMMUNICATION red, FOOD PRODUCTION red, PRINTING yellow, the rest green. South: Commander's Office with a fixed log reader. East: Commander's Quarters, with a HyperSecurity safe (8000-setting dial, 12-20 numbers) and a log tape, which I took. Floyd wandered off "exploring". In the reader, the log so far: fuel cells were locked in the Dome's storage bin, the KEY is in the safe; an alien craft with a dead alien and a featureless pyramid was towed to Docking Bay #1; Shady Dan in the village sells forged Patrol ID cards; the alien course is possibly extra-galactic. Reading the log one "More" at a time is a pleasure.

**Commands 97-110.** Rest of the log: the village is off limits, no more village entry forms will be validated; someone validated a batch, so the Commander hid the STAMP UNDER HIS BED; the pyramid went to the holding tank in the Sci Sub-Module; sabotage-like breakdowns in gym and laundry machinery, a web-feeder, a hull welder; the Duffy's request for my binder forms; then "What the krip!..." and silence. I wasted a click on "Take" for the reader (meant the tape). In the Quarters, bed > More > Look under: a validation stamp! Took it. An explosion nearby: the log reader is now "a black scar" (tape gone with it). South of the office: Briefing Room; west: South Connection, another iris hatch with a slot (no Diplomatic Sub-Module).

**Commands 111-118.** West of South Connection: the Robot Shop, with Oliver, a newborn robot not yet awake (Floyd's speech about waking up lonely moved me), and a heating chamber holding a medium drill bit. My hand would not fit, so I told Floyd to take it; he dropped it hot on the deck, it cooled, I took it: +3, score 8. North of South Connection: South Junction. SW of that the File Room is pitch dark. Met Plato, an older, poetry-reading robot; he and Floyd went off playing Hider-and-Seeker. NE is East Junction, joining the ring. Level Five is a ring: lobby W, North Junction, East Junction, South Junction.

**Commands 119-128.** Asked Plato about himself: he keeps the library. NE of North Junction is the PX: a Vendo-Matic; every item costs 1 galakmid and only #6 All-Purpose Timer and #9 Large Drill Bit are not sold out. I have no coin. West of the PX: North Connection, where a tube leads north to the Scientific Sub-Module (west is the dark Storage). Tube > Engineering Lab (gangways up and down, door north) > Engineering Office: Professor Schmidt's diary. The pyramid is probably over a billion years old, from a neighbouring galaxy; the alien wall dots are a series of identical dots with "nonvisual properties"; "my pal, the mayor, will get to show off his linguistic training." Lab machinery kept failing. Kept the diary.

**Commands 129-141.** The Sci Sub-Module is a stack: Scientists' Quarters (top, nothing found), Astro Lab (took a twenty-prong fromitz board) with Astro Office north (nothing), Engineering Lab + Office, then Bio Lab below with a gangway further down. Bio Office: a scribbled, blood-stained note: "think of this station as a cell and the pyramid as a mechanized bacterioph[age]". Chilling; I now believe the pyramid is behind the breakdowns. The Inventory button began warning "(a take may fumble)", a gentle hint that my hands are full, so I left the note and diary in the Bio Office. Lovely touch.

**Commands 142-156.** Below the Bio Lab: Holding Tank Level. The tank's thick wall has been BLASTED OPEN and it is empty: the pyramid is loose. Walked back to Level Five (Floyd and Plato rejoined) and climbed the ladder to Level Four: barracks N and S, Docking Bay #3 west, elevator east, ladder up/down. Female Barracks: the compass shows N/NE/NW as "special"; they are just empty cubicles. Barracks SanFac (showers, sinks; the fixture offers Turn on / Get in), then Male Barracks, same layout.

**Commands 157-169.** Docking Bay #3 (west of Level Four): a lilac nanofilm spool, taken. Up the ladder to Level Three: doors N, S, NW, doorway SW. North is the Gym: an exercise machine and a sign: its diagnostics talk on FREQUENCY 710, "do not bring anything which broadcasts on that frequency within range." I did not climb in. South is the Theatre with a projection booth and a lock; both "Totally ordinary looking", a flat answer for something that "dominates the room". I began to feel weary; a Sleep button appeared. Floyd spoke sadly of Lazarus and Plato comforted him. I am very fond of these two.

**Commands 170-180.** NW of Level Three: the Laundry: a dryer (empty once opened; "Look inside" told me to open it first, fair), a presser (off, closed), and an empty spot where the washer should be. SW: the Chapel: pulpit, an eternal flame, and a seven-pointed star "blinking with a gentle, rhythmic light", out of reach. Blinking... like the alien dots? Took a puce nanofilm spool and put it in the survival kit; the kit was then full for the lilac one. Still weary.

**Commands 181-193.** Up from Level Three: the Mess Hall, with a still-steaming cup of coffee and no one in sight. Drinking it: "You're neither hungry nor thirsty." Then Welder Number 3 rolled toward me, extensions "quivering with...excitement?" I fled down the ladder and heard it move off. Saved (new position). Now "really tired", I went to the Female Barracks, got into a bed and slept. Day 2 (Novem 5, 11349): woke refreshed, +3, score 11, Floyd calling me a lazy bones. I had dropped everything while asleep; Take all picked it up (and tried to lift Floyd: a surprised squeal; "you decide not to try lifting Plato." Ha.)

**Commands 194-203.** Auto-doors are now "sluggish" and zoom shut too soon: things are getting worse. Down to Level Six: huge doors NW and SW, smaller doors N and S, ladder further down. North: Auxiliary Barracks (unused) and its SanFac to the east. South: Officers' Quarters A (nothing in the desk), Officers SanFac with bathtubs, Officers' Quarters C, then End of Corridor: another security door with an ID reader (north), doors E and SW. East is the Shipping Room, pitch dark. That is the third dark room (Storage, File Room, Shipping Room). Finding a light is now my top need.

**Commands 204-213.** SW of End of Corridor: Officers' Quarters B. Back at Level Six, NW through the huge door: Docking Bay #1 with the small alien ship. Hungry again, so I ate the gray goo (tree-mold custard). Inside the ship: unsettling angles, an empty pedestal (the pyramid's place), a brittle alien skeleton, and dots on the wall in five lines:
`.. ..` / `.. .... . ... . ... ... . ...` / `.. ... .` / `.... . ... .` / `.. ... .`
"Nonvisual properties", said Schmidt, and the menu offered Taste. Tasting gave a sequence of flavours, one group per letter (copied here exactly):
(sweet/slightly-bitter) (sweet/very-sour) | (sweet/very-sweet) (sour/bland/bland/sour) (very-salty) (very-sweet/bland/sour) (bland) (bland/salty/sour) (bitter/sour/very-sour) (slightly-sour) (bitter/salty/bitter) | (very-sweet/very-salty) (spicy-hot/bland/bland) (very-sweet) | (sour/bland/sour/sweet) (bland) (very-salty/salty/sour) (very-sweet) | (bland/bitter) (bland/sour/very-sour) (very-salty).
My theory: a taste-alphabet; "the mayor" in the village has the linguistic training to translate it.

**Commands 214-223.** The skeleton has "an unusually overdeveloped tongue case": taste-speech confirmed. SW of Level Six: Docking Bay #4, empty. Down the ladder: the Printing Plant, with a mauve spool, and a trash can holding a crumpled ILLEGAL SPACE VILLAGE ENTRY FORM FW-83-Q, "pretty crumpled and not validated". I have the validation stamp! I believe the Laundry presser will flatten it, then I stamp it and feed it to an iris-hatch slot. Dropped the lilac spool in the Printing Plant. NW: Paper Recycling Plant; took a drill holding a small drill bit (the safe? the PX sells a Large Drill Bit for 1 galakmid). Plato finished his book and took Floyd to the library.

**Commands 224-238.** The drill's motor "sounds tired; it may not have much work left". A vibration under my feet filled me with dread. Dropped the bedistor in the Printing Plant and climbed four ladders to the Laundry. Opened the presser, put the crumpled form in, closed it, turned it on: a trickle of steam, then "clouds of steam billowing", then it opened, lurched and slammed shut on my arm. Dead (a chuckle or a burp...). The machines are hostile, like the welder. My last save was on Level Three before sleeping (day 1, score 8), so I restored there and must redo the sleep and the trip down to the Printing Plant. Lesson: save often; never stand by a running machine.

**Commands 239-252.** Redid the night: bed, sleep, a different dream this time (my own promotion ceremony on Tremain; I try to shout "No!"). Woke on day 2, +3, score 11, took everything back, and SAVED (new slot, Female Barracks, day 2). Down the ladders: on Level Six "Welder Number 1" came at me, quivering; I fled straight down to the Printing Plant and it moved off. Ladders seem to be the escape from welders.

**Commands 253-265.** A rhythmic throbbing "like a gigantic mechanical heart" from below the Printing Plant. Dropped the lilac spool and bedistor there; opened the trash can and took the crumpled form. The stamp's menu has a clear "Validate…" entry listing forms: validated the crumpled form ("Done."). Climbed to Level Five and walked to South Connection; the slot refused it: "The form's crumpledness prevents it from sliding into the slot." So it must be flattened: back to the presser, more carefully this time. The form's menus offer no "smooth"/"flatten", which a docent would try first.

**Commands 266-275.** Walked back up to Level Three and saved over my old Level Three slot (now day 2, score 11). In the Laundry: opened the presser, form in, closed, turned it on (trickle of steam) and immediately off, then opened it: "a neatly ironed Illegal Space Village Entry Form FW-83-Q", still validated. No arm lost this time. Floyd and Plato are here, sweet as ever. Next: the iris-hatch slot at South Connection, and into the village.

**Commands 276-288.** Hungry again; ate the second gray goo. Walked to South Connection and put the ironed form in the slot: the hatch irised half open, sparked and stuck, but wide enough. +6, score 17. Saved (over the oldest truck slot). South: weightless (the station's gravity stops at the boundary), a filthy Grimy Passage, then Main Street of the village: "there isn't a soul in sight." Openings up, NE, S, W; SE ramps down. Floyd and Plato stayed behind.

**Commands 289-300.** Village: Travel Agency (west; posters), then the Bank (SE of it, also S of Main Street) with a floating platinum detector, which I took and turned on (silent so far; I hope it finds galakmid coins for the PX). Floyd and Plato caught up. NE: the Greasy Straw, a deserted zero-gee diner; NE again the Trading Post, a gutted cargo ship with many exits: a twelve-prong fromitz board and an instruction sheet for FREZONE liquid gorzium explosive (insert in a hole of the right diameter, attach detonator to explosive and timer, set timer, vamoose; keep below 150 K). So: drill a hole in the safe and blow it! Welder Number 1 chased me there; I dropped through the floor to a Warehouse (vacuum storage airlock, "Trespassers will be spaced!"), it followed, I fled SW into an Alley with exits everywhere.

**Commands 301-311.** Alley north: the Missionary's home (an end-of-the-universe kook; empty). Alley east: a "Studio" that turns out to be the Junk Yard (nice joke). Magnetic spaceboots float there; reaching for them, the game warned that my ID card would be wiped if carried with them (no second warning), so I left them. Dropped the explosive instruction sheet there. Up: Shady Dan's office, with a jerry-built "innocuous machine" (keypad, small slot). Saved first. Turned it on, put my ID card in: "Current rank is 6: Lieutenant First Class. Enter new rank." Typed 9: "New rank is 9: HyperAdmiral." Took the card back. Security doors, here I come.

**Commands 312-320.** P.A.: "Deep-space communication received at Comm Center. No operator on duty." (Worth reading the Comm Center screen.) Trading Post sign: "Illegal wares shown by appointment only. FREZONE (tm) explosive available." North: a bare Grocery with a closed plastic bag; opened it: vacuum taffy. Took it (fumble warning returned), so I tucked my ID card back into the uniform. North again: Broadway, a cheap tube with openings in nearly every direction, including down.

**Commands 321-330.** Off Broadway: north a Recruitment Office (rose-coloured posters only); NE a Rec Shop with metallic-green simulation booths (off; I kept clear of machines); east a mining Field Office where a miner left a HEADLAMP. Dropped the twenty-prong fromitz board there to free a hand, took the headlamp and wore it. Now the dark rooms (Storage, File Room, Shipping Room) can be visited. Floyd and Plato keep finding me.

**Commands 331-339.** Broadway west: a Makeshift Connector leading to the back of the East Connection iris hatch (so the village joins at both the S and E hatches). Broadway SE: an old-fashioned Barbershop, and the platinum detector began "quietly beeping". Looking behind the mirror: affixed. I broke it (a docent hesitates over seven years' bad luck!): it dissolved into glass dust and revealed a piece of reflective foil. Took it: +4, score 21. The detector still beeps, so I think the foil itself is the platinum.

**Commands 340-346.** The foil is about two metres square; the beeping followed me, so yes. Broadway SW: a Pet Store with a caged Arcturian balloon creature (hydrogen-filled, smelly) and a leash; its other exit leads SE to the Trading Post. Broadway down: the Fortune Teller's bubble with a crystal ball ("nothing noteworthy"). Here the detector started "getting warm": another machine turning on me, so I dropped it there at once. Still no mayor.

**Commands 347-353.** Broadway NW: "Well, there are openings in ALMOST every direction." (Ha.) A wasted click: I went east from the Grocery into the Barbershop I already knew. Grocery SE: a deserted Saloon, with a partially disguised exit east to a Casino: tables, a spotlit roulette wheel ("nothing eye-catching"), floating dice. Everybody in this village is gone. I am now heading back to the station to try my HyperAdmiral card on the Sick Bay security door.

**Commands 354-363.** Trading Post west: the Studio (the mirror image of the Junk Yard joke), with a J-series hyperdiode in a scrap sculpture (left it). Then Main Street UP: the MAYOR'S OFFICE, with "Deciphering Alien Speech"; opening it dropped the Mayor's translation sheet of taste-words. Matching it to my tasting of the alien dots, I read the wall as:
"Hunji brethren: sabotage failed. However, I have shined light upon the Zeenak weapon's solitary weakness: element 78! Turn back the deadly radiations! The air is souring, however."
Element 78 is PLATINUM. My two-metre platinum foil should turn the pyramid's radiation back on itself. That is the heart of the game, I am sure.

**Commands 364-375.** Left the textbook in the Mayor's Office (kept the translation sheet). Walked back to the station (gravity "tugs you against the deck" again) and saved at South Connection (score 21). To Sick Bay: my HyperAdmiral card in the ID reader opened the security door at once. Behind it: only the Brig, three empty cells ("Totally ordinary looking"). Floyd and Plato bounced in after me. Walked back out; the door works from inside too. The other security door is at End of Corridor on Level Six.

**Commands 376-385.** East Connection's iris hatch is now "frozen open" onto the grimy connector (it was shut on day 1; nothing told me why). The Comm Center screen now shows a message from the Duffy: the binder forms were found in a mislabelled pallet, "Abort assignment and return to Duffy." Ha! But the station is dying: Station Control now shows LIFE SUPPORT, GRAVITY, POWER yellow; COMMUNICATION, FOOD, PRINTING red. Turned on my headlamp and visited the File Room: just octuplet files ("boring does not BEGIN to describe them"). Saved to a new slot here (File Room, day 2, score 21).

**Commands 386-400 (end of leg).** Met Welder Number 4 on Level Five and slipped north through the Workshop door; it moved off. With the headlamp, Storage (N of Workshop) is lit: a JAMMER, a black box with an antenna and TWENTY TINY SOCKETS, settable 0-1400 (was 337). Took it, saved, set it to 710 (the Gym sign's frequency) and turned it on. Walked to the Gym: no visible effect; examining the machine says only "There's no one in the exercise machine." I suspect it needs the twenty-prong fromitz board in its twenty sockets. Saved a new slot in the Gym. The leg ended here, score 21 of 80, day 2.

## Leg handoff

**Where I stopped:** Gym (Level Three), day 2, time 4052, score 21/80, not won. Newest save: "Gym, day 2, score 21". Others: Storage (score 21), File Room (21), South Connection (21), Shady Dan's (17), Level Three (11), Female Barracks (11).
**Carrying:** jammer (ON, set to 710), Mayor's translation paper, reflective platinum foil (2 m square), headlamp (worn, ON), plastic bag with vacuum taffy, medium drill bit, validation stamp, survival kit (puce spool, Thermos of blue soup), Assignment Completion Form, uniform with ID card (now rank 9, HyperAdmiral), chronometer. Floyd and Plato wander and follow.
**Environment note:** my image viewer refused every paper picture, so I never read the three forms or nine blueprints. The course heading came from the session's operator (see commands 45-55), not from the screen.

### Map so far

Duffy (start): Deck Twelve -aft- Forms Storage; -starboard- Cargo Bay Entrance -fore- Robot Pool; -starboard- Cargo Bay (spacetruck).
Station, a stack of levels joined by a central ladder (and an elevator I never used), from top down:
- Level Two: Mess Hall (exits N, S, NE, SE unexplored; steaming coffee).
- Level Three: Gym N, Theatre S (locked projection booth), Laundry NW (presser, dryer), Chapel SW (flame, blinking seven-pointed star out of reach).
- Level Four: Female Barracks N / SanFac / Male Barracks S (beds), Docking Bay #3 W.
- Level Five (ring): lobby; W Docking Bay #2 (my spacetruck); N Workshop - N Storage - E North Connection. NE North Junction: E Sick Bay (security door E to the Brig, empty), NE The PX (vending machine), N North Connection - N Tube to the Sci Sub-Module. East Junction - E East Connection (iris hatch E to the village; S Comm Center; SW Station Control - S Commander's Office: E Commander's Quarters (safe, bed), S Briefing Room - W South Connection). South Junction: SW File Room, S South Connection (iris hatch S to village; W Robot Shop with sleeping Oliver).
- Sci Sub-Module (N of North Connection), top down: Scientists' Quarters; Astro Lab + Office; Engineering Lab + Office; Bio Lab + Office (note, diary dropped there); Holding Tank Level (tank blasted open, empty).
- Level Six: Docking Bay #1 NW (alien ship, dots, skeleton), Docking Bay #4 SW (empty), Auxiliary Barracks N + SanFac, Officers' Quarters A S - SanFac - C - End of Corridor (security door N, unopened; Shipping Room E, dark, unvisited with lamp) - B.
- Level Seven: Printing Plant (trash can, lilac + mauve spools, twenty-ohm bedistor dropped), NW Paper Recycling Plant (drill with small bit, I left the drill there). Ladder continues DOWN ("special"; a throbbing heart-like noise from below).
Village (zero gravity), S of South Connection: Grimy Passage - Main Street: UP Mayor's Office (textbook), W Travel Agency, S/SE Bank, NE Greasy Straw - NE Trading Post (12-prong fromitz board; W Studio with J-series hyperdiode; N Grocery - N Broadway; SE Shady Dan's (rank machine) - down Junk Yard (magnetic boots, explosive sheet) - W Alley; NW Pet Store (balloon creature); E Saloon - E Casino; down Warehouse (vacuum-storage airlock door down, closed). SE/down of Main Street: Alley (N Missionary; S, SE, SW, W unexplored). Broadway: N Recruitment Office, NE Rec Shop (simulation booths), E Field Office (TWENTY-PRONG FROMITZ BOARD dropped here), SE Barbershop, SW Pet Store, W Makeshift Connector to East Connection, down Fortune Teller (platinum detector dropped, it was heating up).

### Puzzles solved

- Pick Floyd: Robot Use form in Robot Pool slot, keypad 3.
- Spacetruck: close hatch first (or you die); sit in pilot seat (Floyd takes copilot), activation form in slot, type the heading. Heading depends on the clock: floor((floor(T/50)-132)^2/4)+103 (operator-supplied); 299 at T=5232. Eat food on arrival.
- Medium drill bit: tell Floyd to take it from the heating chamber. +3
- Validation stamp: under the Commander's bed (from the log tape; the log reader then explodes). Sleep in any bed when tired (+3).
- Village entry: crumpled form from the Printing Plant trash can; Validate it with the stamp; press it in the Laundry presser: turn ON then immediately OFF (waiting kills you); slot at South Connection. +6
- ID card: Shady Dan's machine, turn on, card in slot, type 9 = HyperAdmiral; opens security doors (Sick Bay one done). Do NOT carry the card with the magnetic boots.
- Platinum foil: platinum detector beeps in the Barbershop; break the mirror, take the foil. +4
- Alien message: Taste the dots in the alien ship; translate with the paper in the Mayor's textbook: the pyramid ("Zeenak weapon") is weak to element 78, platinum; "turn back the deadly radiations".

### Open puzzles and theories

- The pyramid is loose somewhere and is turning machines against me (welders, presser, auto-doors, detector heating). Theory: confront it holding the platinum foil to reflect its radiation. Where is it? Likely below the Printing Plant (the throbbing) or behind the End of Corridor security door.
