friction.command: Tell Floyd to > Take > The seven-pointed star (Chapel)
friction.result: "Huh? Floyd shorter even than you!"
friction.why: Funny and fair, and it's nice the Take submenu offers the star so I can try. But it rules out my best theory, and nothing points to the next approach for reaching the star.

friction.command: turn off pulpit switch, then climb pulpit
friction.result: The eternal flame goes out! ... The pulpit sways, and you fall off.

friction.command: turn on headlamp in the dark Shipping Room, read sign
friction.result: Room lights up (pallets of boxes, a big vacant section under a sign). Sign: "Always return the forklift to the shipping room when it's not in use! THIS MEANS YOU!"
friction.why: Perfect environmental clue: the empty spot + sign tells me a forklift exists and is missing, which is exactly the kind of thing that could reach the Chapel star. Also 'headlamp (worn, on)' in the inventory makes the battery-drain risk visible.

friction.command: enter elevator at Printing Plant, keypad 2
friction.result: Shaft has full gravity ('supposed to be weightless... one standard Gee!'), a dread vibration, then on typing 2 the elevator power-dives: You have died.
friction.why: In hindsight the gravity line and dread vibration were warnings, and I'd seen the vibration before without consequence. But the elevator worked for me last leg, the open door invited me in, and dying instantly with no chance to react cost my progress since the last save.

friction.command: turn on Food Processing and Dispensing Unit (Mess Hall)
friction.result: Cheery voice announces sausage, frobbled eggs and teakberry juice... then a hatch opens and a stream of acid shoots out; I leap aside as it etches the floor.
friction.why: Great dark-comedy beat and it fits the sabotage story, but I'm hungry with no food in this save, and the one obvious food source is now off the table.

friction.command: north (and the Compass says S is 'special') in the Dome

friction.command: walk through station auto-doors (Commander's Office, Main Storage, Docking Bay #3...)

friction.why: Nice escalating-dread detail that the station is failing, and it never actually blocks me. It does repeat on almost every door now, so it gets a bit samey.

friction.command: drink cup of coffee (Mess Hall, while hungry and thirsty)
friction.result: "Aaarghhh! The coffee is poisoned! It's eating away at your insides!!" You have died.

Instant death with no smell/look warning when it's the only drink around feels unfair (though in hindsight the acid-spraying dispenser right next to it was a hint).

friction.command: eat taffy (directly from the floating bag, without taking it)

friction.command: read red sign over the Warehouse's down door
friction.result: "TRADING POST VACUUM STORAGE AREA / Trespassers will be spaced!"
friction.why: Ties together the Frezone 'keep below 150 K' warning and the 'by appointment' sign: the illegal stock is out in the cold vacuum. Clear direction without spelling it out.

friction.result: "As you turn the roulette wheel, exits appear above you and to the north!" +4 points, score 32.
friction.why: Reliable, fun payoff for poking at casino stuff, and the compass updates right away with the two new exits.

friction.command: open Flophouse locker; put jammer in locker; take space suit; wear suit
friction.result: Locker reveals a space suit; jammer stashed; suit taken and worn. The '(a take may fumble)' tag on Inventory disappeared after stashing the jammer.
friction.why: The fumble tag acts as a live weight meter, so I knew exactly when I had room for the suit instead of guessing and dropping things by accident.

friction.command: enter Airlock; check survival kit and Thermos menus
friction.result: Stencil: "SECURE ALL OPEN CONTAINERS BEFORE DEPRESSURIZATION." Kit and Thermos menus both offer Close (so they're open); Close kit worked. Floyd: "I'll wait here; ... no room in that phone booth for both of us."
friction.why: The menus tell me open/closed state without a separate examine, so obeying the stencil was easy. Floyd's line explains why he won't follow, nice touch.

friction.command: open airlock outer door (wearing space suit, inner door closed, containers secured)
friction.result: "the air in the lock whooshes out into the vacuum of space, taking you along for the ride." Lost in Space ... your air runs out. You have died.
friction.why: I did everything the stencil asked and wore the suit, and still died instantly. Nothing in the airlock hinted I needed something to hold me down (my guess now: the magnetic boots). A 'you'd better hang on to something' warning or a grab-chance would have been fairer.

friction.command: take magnetic boots in Junk Yard (ID card already dropped), wear boots
friction.result: Taken. You're now wearing the pair of magnetic boots.
friction.why: Easy once I'd figured out why the suit alone killed me. Dropping the card first was painless thanks to last leg's harness warning about boots wiping cards.

friction.command: open airlock outer door wearing suit + magnetic boots
friction.result: "As the door opens, the air in the lock whooshes out into the vacuum of space." (no death this time)
friction.why: Boots confirmed as the fix; the same message minus 'taking you along for the ride' is a clean way to show the difference.

friction.command: go down into the vac yard, turn on headlamp, take explosive
friction.result: +3 (score 35). Lit room: villagers' 'vac yard', items tethered for cold storage; 'you discover a tiny cylinder with an even tinier label' -> explosive… (new). Taken.
friction.why: The headlamp 'swivel' reveal and the (new) tag make the key item pop. Points for just getting out here felt earned after the boots puzzle.

friction.command: open kit; put explosive in Thermos bottle; close bottle (in the vacuum airlock)
friction.result: Done. Inventory nests explosive inside the Thermos inside the kit; bottle closed.
friction.why: Thermos as cold storage for a must-stay-below-150K explosive felt like a genuine survival-crafting 'aha', and the nested inventory confirms it worked.

friction.command: go to Bank looking for a galakmid coin
friction.result: "This is a branch office of the First Galactic Bank of Nebulon." Only a validation stamp floating here; no teller, vault or coins to interact with.
friction.why: A bank is the obvious place for money; finding it totally empty with nothing to open or search was a letdown for a loot hunter who needs one coin for the PX timer.

friction.command: read textbook 'Deciphering Alien Speech' (Mayor's Office), then read the piece of paper
friction.result: A paper flutters out: a glossary pairing tastes (bttr/salty/sweet/sour/blnd/spicy-hot) with meanings like 'legal destruction (sabotage?)', 'bad/evil/deadly radiations', 'weapon (possesv.)', '78 (?) 7/8 (?)'.
friction.why: Huge payoff: it explains Schmidt's 'nonvisual properties' (the alien dots are TASTED) and hints at sabotage and a weapon. Auto-taking the book and the paper on Read saved clicks.

friction.result: Arcturian balloon creatures: filled with hydrogen, float freely like small dirigibles, docile... (plus a recalled fact: they propel themselves with digestive gas, very smelly).
friction.why: Instantly connects to the Chapel: a floating creature could reach the star, and 'hydrogen' explains why the pulpit has a switch to turn off the eternal flame. Great cross-room clue.

friction.command: take leash (Pet Store; first try 10248 failed as menu had closed, then '10236 take')
friction.result: "...it farts right in your face. In a reflexive maneuver to wave away the odor, you release the leash and drop everything you were holding."
friction.why: Hilarious, totally on-brand for a teen. But dropping my whole inventory (including the explosive Thermos!) with no warning is scary; luckily nothing broke. The closed-menu miss cost no turn.

friction.command: take leash again with empty hands; tell Floyd to take leash
friction.result: Same fart; note: "(It will do this every time here. Perhaps it would behave differently somewhere with gravity.)" Floyd: "Enough talking! Let's play Hider-and-Seeker."
friction.why: The explicit gravity hint is helpful, but I can't see any way to get the creature into gravity: the cage has no Take or Put-in, and Floyd ignores the order. Feels like a step is missing from the menus.

friction.result: "Well, there are openings in ALMOST every direction." Now marked '(tried)'.
friction.why: Cute joke, but the Compass button presents it as a real exit labelled 'special', the same label used for actual special exits (iris hatches), so I wasted a turn. Second time this leg (Dome too).

friction.command: walk around the village with the explosive sealed in the Thermos (~45 turns after packing it)
friction.result: "(Even sealed in the Thermos bottle, the explosive is getting softer.)"
friction.why: Clear, early warning that the Thermos only buys time, and it fires while there's still time to react. But nothing earlier hinted the Thermos was only temporary, so I spent those turns hunting a coin instead of heading for the safe.

friction.command: carry Thermos+explosive back to the airlock; open Thermos; drop it in the vac yard; headlamp on to check
friction.result: Warning upgraded: "the explosive is melting: the Thermos bottle only slows it." After dropping: "You can see a Thermos bottle floating here. It seems that the Thermos bottle contains an explosive."
friction.why: The escalating warnings gave me just enough time to bring it back, and the floating Thermos stays put in the vac yard, so I can park it until I have a timer. Costly round trip (~20 commands) though.

friction.command: search Pet Store ceiling; open ceiling panel
friction.result: "you notice something that a casual inspection ... would never have uncovered: a panel mounted in the ceiling." Opening it reveals a stick of ostrich nip.
friction.why: The letter at Doc's ('you'll find it in my ceiling panel') pointed right here, and Search on the generic 'ceiling' object paid off. Great clue chain, and exactly the kind of hidden stash a loot hunter loves.

friction.command: give ostrich nip to ostrich (Doc Schuster's)
friction.result: "The ostrich begins gleefully pecking at the nip, accidentally swallows it, staggers around for a bit, and then finally keels over into a grinning pile of intoxicated ostrich."
friction.why: Funny and satisfying; the Give menu offered the ostrich directly. Not yet sure what knocking it out unlocks.

friction.command: explore Alley SW; read spray can
friction.result: Pawn Shop: someone pawned a spray can. "E-Z SPRAY SPORZ (tm) / A mixture of high-quality spores / Lowest gas-inducement levels of any brand!"
friction.why: Perfect callback to the Pet Store sign (balloon creatures eat airborne spores; they fart to move). Clearly the fix for the leash problem; satisfying cross-room puzzle design.

friction.command: spray can (Pet Store, balloon creature present)
friction.result: "A dusty mist puffs from the can and begins dissipating. The Arcturian balloon creature begins darting around the room, its mouth absurdly wide open."
friction.why: Clear visible reaction confirming the spores are the right item. Welders keep showing up during multi-step puzzles though, forcing me to leave and come back.

friction.command: take leash after spraying spores (Pet Store)
friction.result: Same fart-and-drop-everything message plus "(It will do this every time here. Perhaps it would behave differently somewhere with gravity.)"
friction.why: Feeding it didn't change anything here, and I still can't find a way to get it to gravity (cage has no Take/Put-in, Floyd won't take the leash). Two clue items (spores, gravity hint) but no visible next action; I'm giving up on it for now.

friction.command: Taste pattern of dots (Alien Ship), decode with the Mayor's glossary
friction.result: Taste sequences that decode to: 'Hunji brethren: sabotage failed. However, I have shined light upon the Zeenak weapon's solitary weakness: element 78! Turn back the deadly radiations! The air is souring.'
friction.why: Brilliant multi-room puzzle: Schmidt's 'nonvisual properties' + the glossary + a Taste verb right in the dots menu. Every taste-word matched the glossary exactly, so decoding by hand was fair and fun. Element 78 = platinum = my reflective foil.

friction.result: "A few rungs down, you discover that the ladder passage to Level Eight is sealed off -- apparently from below."
friction.why: Great ominous clue: something on Level 8 sealed itself in. Tells me where the pyramid probably is, even though I can't go that way.

friction.command: enter elevator at Printing Plant (shaft has gravity again), keypad 8
friction.result: "the elevator begins plunging down the shaft in a power dive! You punch frantically at the keypad..." You have died.
friction.why: Second elevator death across legs. With the ladder to Level 8 sealed, the sabotaged elevator looks like the only way down, but every keypad number kills you instantly; I can't tell what I'm supposed to fix first (gravity in the shaft?).

friction.result: "You merely find a few personal items of little interest."
friction.why: Every bedroom (barracks, officers, scientists) has the same bed/cubicle/wardrobe/desk set with the same empty response; for a loot hunter that's a lot of clicks for nothing. A one-line 'nothing useful in any of the quarters' signal would save time.

friction.result: brief romance simulation on San Cupidor, booth shuts off
friction.why: funny payoff for poking at a booth, but no loot; 'Use' quietly mapped to turn on, which was handy

friction.result: ID card twitches toward the magnetic boots; game leaves it rather than wiping it, and warns once
friction.why: saved my ID card from a dumb Take-all accident; clear one-time warning

friction.command: 501 Take (card from Dan's machine, welder 'almost upon you')
friction.result: welder arc kills me
friction.why: welder gives 3 warnings then kills; fair but I had no way to know how many turns I had; costly with the save a few moves back

friction.result: "New rank is 10: Grand Fleet HyperAdmiral."
friction.why: hilarious and a clear win; keypad stayed open with a reminder, card retrieved, fled the welder in time

friction.result: "You'll have to open the counter first." but the counter menu has no Open entry; Look inside then says nothing on the counter
friction.why: game tells me to do something the click menu doesn't offer; wasted a turn with a welder closing in

friction.result: You collapse from extreme thirst and hunger. Died.
friction.why: taffy was flagged as the last food; no food exists after that, so the whole timeline is on a hard clock I can't extend. Warnings were clear though

friction.command: 21 (north through the End of Corridor security door with the rank-10 card)
friction.result: Armory, a fusor-beam zapgun, +5 points (score 33)
friction.why: big payoff: the Dan's-machine card upgrade connects straight to a weapon and points

friction.result: still 'juggling as much as you can manage' - hint had said drop the detonator or survival kit
friction.why: I picked a light item to drop; the limit is weight/bulk, so only the hinted items work. Hint was right but I wasted a turn

triage.name: ROUND-13-TRIAGE.md
triage.text:
# Playtest round 13: triage

Generated by `node scripts/playtest-registry.mjs report 13` from playtests/REGISTRY.jsonl and the round's friction JSONL. Do not edit by hand; re-run it.

747 friction rows this round (375 of them praise, counted and not triaged); 372 linked to 95 issues (48 new, 47 repeats); 0 not yet linked.

By tier: 13 A, 7 B, 75 C.

Suggested A/B/C is the registry's guess from the kind (A: build it, B: a deviation for the sponsor, C: leave it as the original). **Norm confirms each one** (`confirm <id> A|B|C`) after checking it against the ZIL and the oracle.

## New issues

| Issue | Title | Area / room | Kind | Rows this round | Rows in all | Rounds | Suggested | Norm confirms | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF-248 | Round 13 vocabulary: marbles, scribbled, recruitment; huge (the door, the lock) and blinking (the star) as adjectives | Parser / Robot Pool | parse | 6 | 6 | 13 | A | A | fixed | D28 item 6 (the standing vocabulary rule), behind the conveniences switch. Words the game prints that s6.z3 lacks or does not fit: MARBLES ("he seems to be playing marbles", DESCRIBE-FLOYD, ship.zil 667-668; interrupts.zil 111), SCRIBBLED (the note's FDESC, station.zil 3241), RECRUITMENT (the room, village.zil 113, 115). HUGE is the 1987 LARGE (ADJ-SYNONYM, globals.zil 8) and BLINKING a 1987 adjective (station.zil 537), but neither fits the thing the text gives it: the auto-door ("the huge door into the station", station.zil 21; ADJECTIVE AUTO, 3007-3011), the strong box's LOCK ("The box has a HUGE lock", village.zil 1597, 1608), the Chapel star ("The star is blinking.", station.zil 1475; ADJECTIVE SEVEN POINTED, 1487-1491). Oracle (seed 1, 2026-10-07): [I don't know the word "marbles."], "scribbled.", "recruitment."; at route step 22 (Docking Bay #2) "You can't see any huge door here!"; "huge lock", "blinking star" the same; ours matched it word for word with the switch off. Built: MARBLES scenery in the Robot Pool, SCRIBBLED the NOTE's adjective, RECRUITMENT the room's adjective there only, LARGE (so HUGE) on AUTO-DOOR and STRONG-BOX, BLINKING on STAR (engine/parser.js CONV_WORDS, CONV_ADJ, CONV_SCENERY, CONV_PLURAL, roomWords; rules/library.js MARBLES-PSEUDO; wiki canon-deviations.md, Round 13). Not LETTERING (village.zil 1450): six letters to the dictionary it is the 1987 LETTER, Doc Schuster's letter (village.zil 1767-1770), so READ LETTER would ask which. Tests: scripts/tests/clicks.mjs SF-248 (on and off), engine.mjs D28 word list. Fixed in working tree, pending commit. Test: /?room=ROBOT-POOL EXAMINE THE MARBLES; /?room=DOCKING-BAY-2 EXAMINE THE HUGE DOOR; /?room=LOAN-SHARK EXAMINE THE HUGE LOCK; /?room=CHAPEL EXAMINE THE BLINKING STAR; /?room=BIO-OFFICE READ THE SCRIBBLED NOTE; /?room=RECRUITMENT-OFFICE SEARCH THE RECRUITMENT OFFICE. |
| SF-249 | Harness: the package papers were shown only as images, so a tester who cannot view one could not read the course chart (and guessed the heading) | Harness / Spacetruck | blocked | 13 | 13 | 13 | A | A | fixed | Interface (the harness and the tester's tools), not the game: the form text is the 1987 package's, never the game's (READ on a package form is "This form can be found in your STATIONFALL package.", as s6.z3). The round-13 Copilot testers could not view images, so three of three guessed the course: r13-click-fullA typed 285 at 5232 (row 5200-5249: 299) and stranded, then 777, then 299; r13-typed-full typed 285 at 5751 (row 5750-5799: 175), stranded and restarted from the opening at command 49; r13-click-fullB stranded on 285, 777 and 359 before zoomed crops loaded. Fixed in two parts: the text transcriptions of every paper, design/papers/text/<scan name>.md (commit 99ce75cc, after the round started; the QX-17-T table checked against verbs.zil 2140-2152, all 106 rows), copied into a tester's scratch as papers\ (playtests/README.md, Blindness); and now the harness names the text beside the image: showPaper copies design/papers/text/<same name>.md into <session>-papers and says "or read its text transcription (the same paper, word for word) <path>"; --paper (whole and --zoom) names it too (scripts/playtest.mjs paperText). Tests: scripts/tests/playtest.mjs "round 13: the paper viewer names the text transcription..." and "--paper names the text transcription too". Fixed in working tree, pending commit (the harness half; the text files are in 99ce75cc). Test: node scripts/playtest.mjs --session t13p --new --checkpoint 01-duffy, then "read assignment form" (the line names FORM1-QX-17-T.md). Round 13 (later legs): 9 more (r13-click-fullA#196, #197, #199, #210, #211, #212; r13-click-fullB#152, #153, #160). Not back: these legs ran after the fix (2026-10-07 12:09Z on), and the harness named the text transcription; both runs had restarted from the opening and guessed again from the station's address (777, 5959, 7779, 59, 79, and the clock 5688), and r13-click-fullA#212 then found the table "on the Assignment Completion Form's Additional Data slip all along". The course is the 1987 package's copy protection (verbs.zil 2140-2152). C for these rows. |
| SF-250 | The course typed at 5004 stranded the truck though the chart's 5000-5049 row says 359: the course is read at the clock before the TYPE move (4997, row 375) | Duffy / Spacetruck | bug | 2 | 2 | 13 | A | C | left | Not a port bug: the tester read the clock after the TYPE move. V-TYPE in the truck (SPACETRUCK-TYPE, verbs.zil 2125-2152) reads INTERNAL-MOVES as it stands during the command; the move's C-ELAPSED is added after (misc.zil 362). Replaying r13-click-fullB's sent commands (seed 20494) through our engine: after RESTORE (command 59) the status line read 4997; TYPE 359 (command 60) set RIGHT-COURSE 375 ((4997/50-132)^2/4+103 = (99-132)^2/4+103 = 375, the chart's 4950-4999 row) and COURSE-PICKED 359, and the clock then read 5004, the number the diary used ("Restored to my pre-heading save (time 4997), typed 359 at time 5004", r13-click-fullB.md line 28). The later success: status 5276 before TYPE 285 (command 75), RIGHT-COURSE 285 (row 5250-5299), so both readings agreed there. Oracle (s6.z3, seed 24, route to PUT CLASS FORM IN SLOT, status 4995): TYPE 375 docks (+5), TYPE 359 strands ("dead stop in space"); our engine identical. No status-line mismatch (the harness shows INTERNAL-MOVES, as the 1987 status line's MOVES, misc.zil 362-368) and no restore interaction (RESTORE put back 4997 and COURSE-PICKED 0). The route's own note already says "status time before TYPE" (porting/route-seed1.cmds). C: the original. Regression test pinning it: scripts/tests/duffy.mjs "round 13: RIGHT-COURSE at 4997 is 375...". Test: /?checkpoint=01-duffy, read the status-line time, type the chart's course for that time. Round 13 (later legs): 1 more (r13-click-fullB#158: 285, right earlier, stranded at another time). The original: the right course is the chart's row for the clock at the TYPE (verbs.zil 2125-2152). C. |
| SF-251 | Harness: "<keypad> Autopilot keypad" says answer "569 <number>", and "569 285" is then refused as "the menu has closed" | Harness / Spacetruck | confusing | 1 | 1 | 13 | B | A | fixed | Interface (the click harness). "<keypad> Autopilot keypad" with no number reaches the pad's refusal, 'Autopilot keypad: answer "569 <number>"', but unlike SF-139's refusal it left the keypad's menu closed (a turn had closed it, SF-046), so "569 285" was refused as "in the keypad menu, which has closed" (r13-click-fullA transcript lines 57-58; the tester reopened it and typed at line 59). Fixed: that refusal makes the pad's menu the open one (scripts/playtest.mjs resolveClick, the control branch), so the answer it asks for works. The page itself is unaffected (its pad opens in place). Test: scripts/tests/playtest.mjs "round 13: \"<keypad> <pad>\" with no number..." (checkpoint 02-station: wait, "<keypad> autopilot keypad", then "<pad> 6" types 6). Fixed in working tree, pending commit. |
| SF-252 | East Connection's iris hatch is "shut tight" on one visit and "frozen open" on the next, with no event seen there | Level Five / East Connection | confusing | 2 | 2 | 13 | B | C | left | The original. There is one IRIS-HATCH (village.zil 34-40), a GLOBAL of both East Connection (station.zil 476) and South Connection (1093); the validated entry form opens it at either (FORM-SLOT-F, globals.zil 735-744, FSET IRIS-HATCH OPENBIT), and East Connection then reads "frozen open, revealing not a sub-module connector but a small, grimy connector" (station.zil 485-488). r13-click-fullA opened it at the South Connection (command 281, "The hatch begins irising open, then sparks and smokes and grinds to a halt"), and saw the East's next on command 376. C (a B would add a line the 1987 game never prints). Round 13 (later legs): 1 more (r13-click-fullA#18, the same sighting on a later visit). Still the original (village.zil 34-40; station.zil 476, 485-488, 1093; globals.zil 735-744). |
| SF-253 | Pitch-black rooms (Storage, File Room, Shipping Room) with no light source found after six levels | Station / Shipping Room | blocked | 5 | 5 | 13 | A | C | left | The original: Storage (STORAGE-5, FLAGS RLANDBIT, station.zil 75-83), the File Room (681) and the Shipping Room (2620) have no ONBIT, so they are dark ("It is pitch black.", verbs.zil 2668); the light is the miner's headlamp in the village Field Office (HEADLAMP, IN FIELD-OFFICE, village.zil 210-214). The tester found it 60 commands later (r13-click-fullB.md, commands 306-320: "Now the dark rooms ... are open to me"). C. Round 13 (later legs): 4 more (r13-click-fullA#134, #150, #172; r13-click-fullB#165). Still the original (station.zil 75-83, 681, 2620; verbs.zil 2668); the headlamp is in the Field Office (village.zil 210-214). |
| SF-254 | TAKE INVENTORY: [You used the word "inventory" in a way that I don't understand.] | Parser / Deck Twelve | parse | 1 | 1 | 13 | A | C | left | The original. Oracle (seed 1, start): TAKE INVENTORY is "[You used the word "inventory" in a way that I don't understand.]"; ours the same with the switch on and off. INVENTORY is a verb word only (SYNTAX INVENT, syntax.zil 42; SF-226 made it a noun in the vac yard alone). Not a D28 item-6 word: the game never prints "take inventory". The tester typed INVENTORY next. C. |
| SF-255 | A thing named by where it is is not a sentence: READ THE WRITING ON THE BOXES, READ THE LETTERING ON THE SPRAY CAN, READ THE SIGN ON THE BIN, EXAMINE THE ROBOT IN THE THIRD BIN | Parser / Forms Storage Room | parse | 6 | 6 | 13 | A | B | open | The original refuses each the same way. Oracle (seed 1): READ THE SIGN ON THE BIN and READ THE LETTERING ON THE CAN are "[That sentence isn't one I recognize.]" (READ takes THROUGH and WITH, never ON: syntax.zil 437-440), and so is EXAMINE THE ROBOT IN THE THIRD BIN at the Robot Pool (route step 2); READ THE WRITING ON THE BOXES is [I don't know the word "writing."] in s6.z3 and, with SF-154's WRITING, "[That sentence isn't one I recognize.]" in ours. Ours matches the oracle in each. The bare forms work (READ BOXES, READ WRITING with the switch on, READ SPRAY CAN, READ SIGN, EXAMINE THIRD ROBOT). Four rows in one typed run (#2, #3, #19, #22). As the original, C; the fix would be grammar the 1987 parser never had, so it is a B: (a) leave it (C); (b) with the conveniences on, READ or EXAMINE <writing \| lettering \| sign \| words \| label> ON <thing> acts on the thing, and EXAMINE <thing> IN <container> on the thing when it is in that container (the robot in the third bin, Floyd), behind the D12 switch, marked as a D28-style deviation; (c) (b) plus a one-time hint after the refusal: "(Try READ <the thing>.)". Recommendation: (b), the phrasings the room texts invite ("Each box has some writing stamped on the side", ship.zil 183; "has some lettering on it", village.zil 1450; "the robot in the third bin", ship.zil 667). Default: (a), the original, until the sponsor answers. Round 13 (later legs): 2 more (r13-typed-full#51, READ THE WRITING ON THE BOXES again; #270, READ THE MESSAGE ON THE SCREEN, "[That sentence isn't one I recognize.]"; READ THE SCREEN works). Same B; the batch below already carries it. |
| SF-256 | A line of several sentences is thrown away whole when the first is not understood, with no word of which part failed | Parser / Dome | parse | 0 | 0 | 13 | A | C | left | The original. Oracle (seed 1, Robot Pool): "READ THE SIGN ON THE BIN. LOOK." prints only "[That sentence isn't one I recognize.]" and LOOK never runs: on a parse failure the 1987 parser drops the rest of the line (P-CONT cleared when the parse fails, misc.zil 359-360). Ours the same. The error names no sentence, as the original's. Raised by r13-typed-full#22 (linked to SF-255, its first sentence). C. |
| SF-257 | Two actions joined by AND (STAND UP AND OPEN THE HATCH): [You used the word "open" in a way that I don't understand.] | Parser / Spacetruck | parse | 2 | 2 | 13 | A | C | left | The original. Oracle (seed 1, Deck Twelve): STAND UP AND OPEN THE HATCH is "[You used the word "open" in a way that I don't understand.]", word for word ours. The 1987 parser joins sentences with THEN or a period, not AND between verbs (AND joins objects). C. Round 13 (later legs): 1 more (r13-typed-full#267: FLOYD, REACH INTO THE HOLE AND TAKE THE TIMER, "[You used the word "take" in a way that I don't understand.]"). Still the original: AND joins objects, not orders. FLOYD, REACH INTO THE HOLE gets FLOYD-F's "Nope, not even a ball." (ship.zil 393-398); the timer comes out with the ostrich (route steps 170-174). |
| SF-258 | Round 13 vocabulary, second batch: emergency and beacon (the red buttons), Zeenak (the pyramid), barbershop, missionary, kook, opening, small (Shady Dan's slot), course and reservoir | Parser / Comm Center | parse | 10 | 10 | 13 | A | A | fixed | D28 item 6 (the standing vocabulary rule), behind the conveniences switch. Words the game prints that s6.z3 lacks or does not fit: EMERGENCY and BEACON ("the red button of the wide-band emergency beacon", COMM-CENTER-F, station.zil 612-613; "a red button for activating the emergency beacon", SPACETRUCK-F, ship.zil 1013; both the PSEUDO RED BUTTON, station.zil 601, ship.zil 1003), ZEENAK ("the Zeenak pyramid", station.zil 3563), BARBERSHOP ("a classic barbershop mirror", village.zil 260; the room, 246), MISSIONARY (the room, village.zil 1138) and KOOK ("the home of some kook", 1140), OPENING ("there's an opening in the floor", the Trading Post, village.zil 564; the Workshop, station.zil 56), COURSE ("Type in the course heading", globals.zil 722), RESERVOIR ("the flame's fuel reservoir, located...", station.zil 2009); SMALL is a 1987 word that does not fit Shady Dan's "very small slot" (ID-CHANGER-F, village.zil 1821; the PSEUDO SLOT, 1794-1805). Oracle (seed 1, 2026-10-08): [I don't know the word "emergency."], "beacon.", "zeenak.", "barbershop.", "missionary.", "kook.", "opening.", "course.", "reservoir."; at route step 92 "You can't see any small slot here!"; ours word for word with the switch off. Built: BEACON the red button's scenery word in the Comm Center and the spacetruck, EMERGENCY and BEACON its adjectives (PUSH THE BEACON shocks as PUSH BUTTON does), ZEENAK the pyramid's adjective, BARBERSHOP the mirror's adjective and the room's word there, MISSIONARY the room's word there, KOOK a topic there (absent: "You can't see any kook here."), OPENING scenery in the Trading Post and the Workshop, SMALL on Dan's slot, COURSE and RESERVOIR topics as MAYOR is (engine/parser.js CONV_WORDS, CONV_ADJ, CONV_PSEUDO_ADJ, CONV_SCENERY, CONV_SAME, roomWords, convPseudos; rules/library.js OPENINGS-PSEUDO, KOOKS-PSEUDO; wiki canon-deviations.md, Round 13 second batch). Not DUFFY or COMMAND (the Command Module): no 1987 object stands for either, and a topic word would answer "You can't see any ... here" aboard the Duffy or inside the Command Module (SF-263).
